statement: Hardware and software are checked as genuine before they are acquired, and software is checked for integrity, for example by signature or hash, before it is installed or used. The source of new software is checked. A record of each check is kept. Proof is the procedure and acquisition and integrity check records.
why_asked: Counterfeit hardware and tampered software arrive already compromised and bypass every later control.
how_to_ask: Ask how a new device or package is confirmed as genuine, then ask for the record of one check. Example probe: "For the last software package you installed, how did you confirm its source and that it was not altered?"
question: Does your organization check that hardware and software are genuine before it acquires or uses them?
expected_evidence: Procedure for authenticity and integrity checks; supplier legitimacy checks; signature or hash verification records for installed software; acquisition records; covering the audit period
good_looks_like: A procedure requires authenticity checks before acquisition and integrity checks before use. The source of new software is checked. Recent acquisitions show the checks were done and recorded before deployment.
test: Obtain the procedure and the acquisition and integrity check records. Sample five recent acquisitions of hardware or software and check each has a recorded authenticity or integrity check before deployment. Pass if all sampled items have a record.
baseline_risk: Counterfeit or tampered products enter the environment with built-in backdoors or malware.
